title: Okinawa: bombed landscape and thirty days of Spam
summary: Supplies failed so they ate C-rations and Spam on Okinawa among shot-off trees and empty highways, and he was eager to go home.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: There wasn't too much to talk about at Okinawa, except the food supply didn't come in, and we had to eat C-rations and Spam, the Spam that they told us we would eat til it run out of our ears... But we did on Okinawa. We ate Spam just about thirty days. That was bad. That was the bad part of the trip.

But other than that, it was a wonderful sight to see; you know, see them bombed-out places and one-thing-or-another. It was really history. But Lord have mercy, I wouldn't want to go through it again. And Okinawa, all the trees... All the tops were shot off the trees. You'd just see the tree stumps standing up there, and all the tops were shot off. Some of the most beautiful highways in the world was in Okinawa, which the American soldiers had built. But there was nothin' around! There were highways, but there were no houses, no nothin' -- there was nothin' whatsoever. Everywhere. If you wanted to go anywhere, the nearest place you could go would be about ten miles away. They didn't have any transportation. They had ...(?)...

I mean, there was really nothing to do in Okinawa. But we made the thirty days, and then they told us we were going to Japan. I said, 'Damn, about time. You're five months with that Japan.' You know, I had lost all the enthusiasm about Japan. I wanted to come home.
